title: TTL Book Talk:  Arthur Brooks, Love Your Enemies

location.venue: St. Louis County Library - Clark Family Branch

description:
Wonder how we got to such a dysfunctional political climate? Arthur Brooks explains it in this timely book, Love Your Enemies: How Decent People Can Save America From the Culture of Contempt. Though his book was published in 2019, his concerns are accelerating and at a tipping point! Find answers to how we got here and how we can heal the political divide. Join us for an overview and discussion of Arthur Brooks’ informative and essential book!

Protests, strikes, boycotts are all useful tools in our effort to halt efforts to destroy democracy. But, something as powerful, is the simple art of conversation in civil discourse. Like a pebble in the pond, talk can emanate outward, bringing people into action, who might not have a bigger picture. Talk, stories, and recognizing common ground in one another, can get us there.

Overview of the book (Just in case you didn’t get the whole thing read!)

Breakout discussions on chapters that spoke to us most

Practice conversations of how to engage someone of a different political perspective

How to handle a counter protestor - bridging the divide and deescalation

How to talk to others in your own life. - (We all have at least, that one person.)

Next steps . . . A plan to implement what we have learned from Brooks in our own lives

description:
Join us for a rally to bring together Brazoria County in defense of our rights and our community.

title: March with Labor in World Pride!
description:
Pride At Work and the labor movement stand in solidarity with all of our LGBTQIA+ siblings under attack for who we are and who we love across the world and here in the United States.

With World Pride 2025 in Washington, D.C., we unite as the Labor and LGBTQIA+ movements to say loud and clear:
We are not afraid. We protect our trans and immigrant siblings. We are building a future together where all of us can live and work with safety, respect, and authenticity!

Featured speakers include AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler, RWDSU President Stuart Appelbaum, and workers from Starbucks Workers United, the UAW Kennedy Center campaign, and more!

Wear your union and Pride At Work shirts, hats, buttons, etc!

Public transportation, comfortable walking shoes, sunscreen, and water are strongly recommended. Backpacks and bags are prohibited. Personal items may be carried in a clear plastic bag.

Parking availability and access in downtown D.C. shouldn't be expected this weekend due to World Pride crowds and street closures, but if you must drive we suggest trying Colonial Parking.

Please note that the Sunday 6/8 March is different from the Saturday 6/7 Parade!

description:
Nonviolent Direct Action/CD training (5 hours)
Civil disobedience is a principled, time-honored, public, and effective method of bringing fierce nonviolent pressure to bear on unjust systems. This training -- with a break for lunch -- introduces people to the philosophy and techniques of nonviolence and direct action; how affinity groups and consensus-based decision-making work; arrest and consequences; "solidarity" as a tool for actions, jail, and court; the role of support (legal and non-legal); day-of protest tips.

Alexis Danzig has trained hundreds of people to participate in principled direct action and nonviolent civil disobedience since joining ACT UP NY in 1988.

After helping to co-found Rise and Resist in response to the 2016 election, Alexis is delighted to travel to communities interested in learning how to organize democratically to resist attacks on cherished American values of freedom and equality and to become braver together in public.

title: Tues. 6/10 > I-91 Overpass Standout - 9 Mtn Park Rd, Holyoke, MA
description:
Come out to show that ordinary people can raise their voices against the chaos and destruction of this Administration. Help remind folks that they, too, can stand up for their beliefs - and that there's lots and lots of people who aren't on board with the "cruelty as entertainment" behavior of Trump and Musk and the GOP.

### Recent DOT Visits

A Department of Transportation employee has visited twice in the past three weeks prior to 5/20 to ask that people NOT attach anything to the fencing. On 5/20, he parked and waited until everything was removed from the fencing. It seems reasonable to expect that DOT enforcement will continue.

### How to Get There

The address "9 Mountain Park Rd, Holyoke" will get you there if you're using Waze. (Mountain Park Road runs off Route 5, and is not accessible from I-91.) People have reported that some GPS systems bring you right under the bridge, but on I-91. That’s annoying!

Please park on the side of the road before the bridge. We can't park on the bridge.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.
